import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu

# Try to import MyGeneInfo, install if necessary
try:
    from mygene import MyGeneInfo
except ImportError:
    import subprocess, sys
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--quiet', 'mygene'])
    from mygene import MyGeneInfo

# 1. Load clinical and gene expression data
clin = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', dtype=str)
expr = pd.read_csv('cleaned_gene_expression.csv', index_col=0)

# 2. Map CD8A to Ensembl ID
mg = MyGeneInfo()
query = mg.query('CD8A', species='human', fields='ensembl.gene')
ensembl = None
for hit in query.get('hits', []):
    eg = hit.get('ensembl')
    if isinstance(eg, dict):
        ensembl = eg.get('gene')
        break
    elif isinstance(eg, list) and eg:
        ensembl = eg[0].get('gene')
        break
if not ensembl:
    raise ValueError('CD8A Ensembl ID not found')

# 3. Extract ulceration status
clin_sub = clin[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'ulceration_indicator']].dropna()
clin_sub = clin_sub[clin_sub['ulceration_indicator'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]
clin_sub = clin_sub.rename(columns={'bcr_patient_barcode': 'patient_id'})

# 4. Extract CD8A expression
# Remove version suffix from Ensembl IDs
expr.index = expr.index.str.split('.').str[0]
if ensembl not in expr.index:
    raise KeyError(f'{ensembl} not in expression data')
cd8a_expr = expr.loc[ensembl]
# 5. Aggregate per patient
cd8a = cd8a_expr.rename('CD8A').reset_index()
cd8a.columns = ['sample_id', 'CD8A']
cd8a['patient_id'] = cd8a['sample_id'].str.slice(0, 12)
cd8a_agg = cd8a.groupby('patient_id')['CD8A'].mean().reset_index()

# 6. Merge clinical and expression data
df = pd.merge(clin_sub, cd8a_agg, on='patient_id', how='inner')

# 7. Summary statistics by group
summary = df.groupby('ulceration_indicator')['CD8A'].agg(
    n='count', mean='mean', median='median', std='std'
).reset_index()
print('Summary statistics by ulceration status:')
print(summary.to_string(index=False))

# 8. Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U)
g1 = df[df['ulceration_indicator'] == 'YES']['CD8A']
g2 = df[df['ulceration_indicator'] == 'NO']['CD8A']
stat, p = mannwhitneyu(g1, g2, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"\nMann-Whitney U test: U={stat:.2f}, p-value={p:.4f}")

# 9. Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.violinplot(x='ulceration_indicator', y='CD8A', data=df, palette='Set2', inner='box')
sns.swarmplot(x='ulceration_indicator', y='CD8A', data=df, color='k', size=2, alpha=0.6)
plt.title(f'CD8A expression by ulceration status (p={p:.4f})')
plt.xlabel('Ulceration Indicator')
plt.ylabel('CD8A expression (log2 FPKM+0.001)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Optionally fit a linear regression model CD274 ~ log2(TMB+1) + age_at_diagnosis + ulceration_indicator and report coefficients.","deliverables":"• Table of patient TMB and CD274 expression values; • Spearman correlation coefficient and p‐value; • Scatter plot with trend line; • Regression model summary (if performed)."}},{"hypothesis":"Breslow thickness is positively correlated with HIF1A (hypoxia inducible factor 1 alpha) expression in SKCM tumors.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Test whether thicker melanomas (higher Breslow thickness) show elevated HIF1A expression, suggesting hypoxia‐driven adaptation.","steps":"1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv. 2. Extract patients with non–missing breslow_thickness and age_at_diagnosis. 3. Map HIF1A to its Ensembl ID; confirm in expression data after stripping version suffix. 4. For each sample, extract HIF1A expression, aggregate to per‐patient mean by barcode prefix. 5. Merge breslow_thickness and HIF1A expression by patient_id. 6. Compute Spearman correlation between breslow_thickness and HIF1A expression and test significance. 7. Create a scatter plot with Breslow thickness on the x‐axis and HIF1A expression on the y‐axis, overlay LOESS or linear fit. 8. Optionally fit a multivariate linear model: HIF1A_expression ~ breslow_thickness + age_at_diagnosis + ulceration_indicator.","deliverables":"• Table of breslow_thickness and HIF1A expression per patient; • Spearman rho and p‐value; • Scatter plot with fit; • Linear model summary (if applied)."}},{"hypothesis":"SKCM patients who received prior radiation therapy exhibit increased expression of the DNA damage response gene GADD45A relative to those without prior radiation.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Evaluate whether prior radiation exposure associates with upregulation of GADD45A, a marker of DNA damage repair activation.","steps":"1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv. 2. From clinical data, select patient_id and prior_radiation_therapy, filter to YES and NO groups, drop missing. 3. Map GADD45A to Ensembl ID; strip version suffix from expression index. 4. Extract GADD45A expression per sample and aggregate to mean per patient_id. 5. Merge clinical prior_radiation_therapy status with GADD45A expression by patient_id. 6. Compute group‐wise summary (n, mean, median, std) for YES vs NO. 7. Perform a Mann–Whitney U test comparing GADD45A expression between groups. 8. Generate boxplot or violin plot of GADD45A expression stratified by radiation status with p‐value annotation.","deliverables":"• Summary statistics table for GADD45A by prior radiation status; • Mann–Whitney U statistic and p‐value; • Boxplot or violin plot of expression by group."}},{"hypothesis":"SKCM tumors harboring the BRAF V600 mutation exhibit higher overall tumor mutational burden compared to BRAF wild‐type tumors.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Determine if BRAF V600–mutant melanoma has a distinct mutational landscape reflected by higher systemic mutation counts.","steps":"1. Load cleaned_mutations.csv and cleaned_clinical_data.csv. 2. In mutations, flag patients with Hugo_Symbol=='BRAF' and HGVSp_Short containing 'V600' as mutant, others as wild‐type. 3. For each patient_id, count total mutations to compute TMB. 4. Create a dataframe with patient_id, BRAF_status, and TMB. 5. Compute summary stats (n, mean, median, std) of TMB for mutant vs wild‐type groups. 6. Perform Mann–Whitney U test comparing TMB between the two groups. 7. Generate boxplot of TMB by BRAF status annotated with p‐value.","deliverables":"• Counts of BRAF V600 mutants vs wild‐type; • Summary statistics of TMB by group; • Mann–Whitney U statistic and p‐value; • Boxplot of TMB stratified by BRAF status."}},{"hypothesis":"Elevated serum LDH (lactate_dehydrogenase_result = Elevated) is associated with reduced expression of a T‐cell signature (average of CD8A, CD3D, CD3E) in SKCM tumors.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Test whether patients with elevated LDH exhibit lower intratumoral T‐cell infiltration signature.","steps":"1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv. 2. From clinical data, select patient_id and lactate_dehydrogenase_result, filter to Elevated, Normal, and drop missing. 3. Identify Ensembl IDs for CD8A, CD3D, and CD3E, confirm presence in expression data. 4. For each sample, extract expression of the three genes, compute per‐sample T‐cell signature as the mean expression, then aggregate to per‐patient signature. 5. Merge LDH status with T‐cell signature by patient_id. 6. Compute group summary stats (n, mean, median, std) for Elevated vs Normal. 7. Perform a Kruskal‐Wallis test across the two groups. 8. Generate violin or boxplot of T‐cell signature by LDH status with p‐value annotation. 9. If significant, perform post‐hoc Dunn’s test to confirm pairwise differences.","deliverables":"• Table of T‐cell signature summary by LDH group; • Kruskal‐Wallis statistic and p‐value; • Post‐hoc test results (if applied); • Plot of signature by LDH status."}},{"hypothesis":"Higher Clark invasion level is associated with increased tumor mutational burden in SKCM patients.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Examine the relationship between histological invasion depth (Clark level) and systemic mutation counts.","steps":"1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_mutations.csv. 2. From clinical data, extract patient_id and clark_level, filter complete cases and order levels II, III, IV, V. 3. From mutations, count total mutations per patient_id to compute TMB. 4. Merge clark_level and TMB by patient_id. 5. Compute per‐level summary (n, mean, median, std) of TMB. 6. Perform Kruskal‐Wallis test to assess differences in TMB across levels. 7. Generate boxplot of TMB by Clark level with overall p‐value. 8. If significant, perform pairwise Wilcoxon tests with Bonferroni correction.","deliverables":"• Summary table of TMB by Clark level; • Kruskal‐Wallis statistic and p‐value; • Pairwise test results (if applied); • Boxplot of TMB vs Clark level."}},{"hypothesis":"Metastatic samples from lymph nodes exhibit lower immune infiltration signature compared to primary skin tumors in SKCM.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Compare immune cell–associated gene expression between lymph node metastases and primary skin tumors.","steps":"1. Extract expression of signature genes per sample, compute per‐sample signature as mean expression, then aggregate to per‐patient mean. 5. Merge tumor location and signature by patient_id. 6. For each sample, extract MITF expression and aggregate to per‐patient mean. 4. Merge MITF expression with survival data: define time = days_to_death if Dead else days_to_last_followup, event=1 if Dead else 0. 5. Dichotomize MITF expression at median into High vs Low. 6. Generate Kaplan–Meier survival curves for High vs Low groups; perform log‐rank test. 7. Fit a multivariate Cox proportional hazards model: survival ~ MITF_group + age_at_diagnosis + ulceration_indicator. 8. Check proportional hazards assumptions using Schoenfeld residuals.","deliverables":"• Counts in MITF High and Low groups; • Kaplan–Meier plot and log‐rank p‐value; • Cox model summary with hazard ratios, 95% CIs, and p‐values; • Diagnostics for proportional hazards assumptions."}}]}
